ONE KNOB: recon_eta 30.0 -> 5.0 (DPS soft-guidance gain DOWN). All else IDENTICAL to iter-1 (n_steps=25, init=fbp, recon_dcstep_every=0 so the hard-CG projection stays OFF -> pure soft DPS; recon_eta_clamp=false). iter-1 NUMBERS (eta=30): SSIM 0.3688, hr=0.0, PSNR 10.55, RMSE 0.01485, 868.65 s / 214 slices = 4.06 s/slice -- FAR BELOW the LD-FBP floor 0.8078 AND below its own FBP init, and below the constrained sibling's 0.3937. FAILURE MODE (shared with the constrained sibling's iter-2 diagnosis): eta is a dimensionless gain in the adaptively-normalized DPS step (step = (eta/||resid||)*grad, Chung 2023 eq.12); the literature/demo/breast default is 1.0, so eta=30 (a leftover discarded-614 boundary-metric hint) is a ~30x overshoot that, with recon_eta_clamp=false (no per-step displacement cap), blows the FBP-initialized iterate OFF-MANIFOLD every reverse step -> the recon is corrupted, not merely prior-dominated drift. DISTINCT FROM THE CONSTRAINED SIBLING (which is running eta 30->1.0 WITH hard-CG every=5): this unconstrained variant has recon_dcstep_every=0, i.e. NO hard-CG fidelity backstop, so the soft DPS gradient is its ONLY data-consistency mechanism -> it needs MORE guidance than the constrained sibling. I pick eta=5.0 (a clearly different magnitude than the sibling's 1.0) so the pair BRACKETS the soft-guidance response: constrained = gentle-soft (eta=1) + hard-CG; unconstrained = moderate-soft (eta=5) + no-CG. BUDGET: eta is a free scalar multiplier on the existing per-step gradient -- no extra forward/backward or projection calls -> per-slice cost stays ~4.06 s; 214 slices * 4.06 s = 869 s = 14.5 min < 20-min (1200 s) wall (~330 s headroom); n_steps unchanged so no budget risk. val=ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV (default). HYPOTHESIS: if I lower eta 30 -> 5, SSIM rises above the iter-1 0.3688 because the gentler-but-still-substantial soft DPS gradient keeps the FBP-initialized iterate on-manifold while still pulling toward the measurements (less off-manifold corruption). FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays ~0.37-0.5 (still << the 0.8078 LD-FBP floor) at eta=5 -- and the constrained sibling likewise fails to clear FBP at eta=1 -- then the DPS step size was NOT the issue: the Mayo v4 DDPM prior is mismatched to the rebinned-Mayo distribution under the 25-step low-T budget (mirrors the breast-DDPM hr=0 structural verdict: globally faithful but not conditionally faithful under DPS). iter-3 would then redirect to n_steps (longer DDIM trajectory) or accept an architectural prior-mismatch ceiling, not the guidance gain.

diffusion_recon_dcstep_unconstrained_mayo_v4-claude-agentic: recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ddpm_mayo_unconstrained_v4.pt, recon_mode=dps, recon_sample_steps=32, recon_eta=5.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=False, recon_dcstep_every=0, recon_dcstep_n_cg=3, recon_dcstep_warmup=5, recon_dcstep_relax=1.0, val_n=214, train_n=0, rationale=iter-3 search-20260619-01 UNCONSTRAINED diff-recon vs reused Mayo DDPM v4 ckpt (ddpm_mayo_unconstrained_v4.pt). ONE KNOB: recon_sample_steps (n_steps) 25 -> 32 (LONGER DDIM reverse trajectory). All else IDENTICAL to iter-2 (recon_eta=5.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_dcstep_every=0 so the hard-CG projection stays OFF -> pure soft DPS; recon_eta_clamp=false; val_n=214). TRAJECTORY iter-1 (n_steps=25, eta=30): SSIM 0.3688, hr=0.0, PSNR 10.55, 868.65s/214 = 4.06 s/slice. iter-2 (n_steps=25, eta=5): SSIM 0.3960, hr=0.0, PSNR 11.25, 868.33s/214 = 4.06 s/slice. The eta 30->5 correction gave a SLIGHT lift (+0.027) but the recon is STILL FAR below the LD-FBP floor 0.8078 (and the constrained sibling REGRESSED on its eta fix eta30->1: 0.39->0.24), so the DPS guidance-gain lever is now EXHAUSTED. FAILURE MODE: the recon is dominated by a Mayo v4 DDPM prior that is MISMATCHED to the rebinned-Mayo distribution under the short 25-step low-T reverse budget -- per findings the prior is globally faithful (plausible CT texture) but NOT conditionally faithful to the input sino under DPS/DC (exactly the breast-DDPM hr=0 structural verdict, where 4x-16x capacity + 2.5x training all stayed in the 0.3-0.5 SSIM band). ONE KNOB JUSTIFICATION: n_steps is the highest-value untried lever -- a longer DDIM reverse trajectory gives the soft-DPS prior more steps to settle from the FBP init toward the measurement manifold; the 25-step low-T budget may simply be too short to converge. BUDGET MATH (HARD 20-min = 1200s wall, val=ALL 214 L277 slices): per-step cost dominates (each of the n_steps reverse iterations does one DDPM-net forward + one projector forward + one autograd backward; dcstep_every=0 so NO extra CG cost), so per-slice cost is ~linear in n_steps with a small fixed FBP-init+IO offset. iter-2 = 4.06 s/slice at 25 steps. At 32 steps (worst-case fully-linear): 4.06*(32/25) = 5.20 s/slice -> 214*5.20 = 1112s = 18.5 min < 1200s wall (~88s headroom, MORE in practice because the fixed offset does not scale). Doubling to 50 steps (8.1 s/slice -> ~29 min) would BLOW the wall, so n_steps=32 (+28% trajectory) is the LARGEST step count that fits with margin -- the right budget-feasible probe, not a naive 2x. HYPOTHESIS: if I extend the DDIM trajectory 25 -> 32 steps, SSIM rises meaningfully above the iter-2 0.3960 because the longer reverse path lets the FBP-initialized iterate relax further onto the sino-consistent mode. FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays well below the FBP floor (~0.4 vs 0.81) even with the longer trajectory, then the Mayo v4 DDPM prior is STRUCTURALLY mismatched (not a step-budget issue) -> file a negative result and STOP iterating diffusion-recon on Mayo (the lever is the prior CLASS, not any sampler hyperparameter, mirroring the breast-DDPM decision).

ONE KNOB: recon_dcstep_every 0 -> 5 (turn ON the hard-CG data-consistency projection inside the otherwise-soft DPS reverse path -- the LAST UNTRIED lever). recon_dcstep_n_cg 3 -> 2 and recon_sample_steps 32 -> 25 are BUDGET-FORCED, not free choices: enabling hard-DC adds n_cg*(2 fwd + 1 back) projector calls per triggered step, so I must shrink the base trajectory to keep the 20-min wall (see BUDGET below); n_steps=25 is exactly the iter-2 base where eta=5 was already well-behaved, so the soft sub-path is held at its settled point and the every:0->5 flip is the only mechanistic change. recon_eta=5.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=false, recon_dcstep_relax=1.0 (FULL hard projection), recon_dcstep_warmup=5 all UNCHANGED. TRAJECTORY (corrected 214-slice / 321px-FOV metric): iter-1 (n_steps=25, eta=30, every=0) SSIM 0.3688 hr=0 PSNR 10.55 868.65s; iter-2 (25, eta=5, every=0) SSIM 0.3960 hr=0 PSNR 11.25 868.33s -- BEST SO FAR; iter-3 (32, eta=5, every=0) SSIM 0.3869 hr=0 PSNR 11.08 1103.8s -- longer DDIM trajectory did NOT help (slightly DOWN). All three sit in the 0.37-0.40 band, FAR below the LD-FBP floor 0.8078 and even below the FBP init. The two soft levers -- DPS guidance gain (eta 30->5) and trajectory length (n_steps 25->32) -- are now EXHAUSTED and FLAT, and the constrained sibling (eta 30->1 + hard-CG every=5) REGRESSED 0.39->0.24, so neither soft guidance nor capacity is the issue. FAILURE MODE (the hypothesis under final test): the recon is dominated by a Mayo v4 DDPM PRIOR that is STRUCTURALLY MISMATCHED to the rebinned-Mayo distribution -- globally faithful (plausible CT texture) but NOT conditionally faithful to the input sino under DPS, exactly the breast-DDPM hr=0 structural verdict (4x-16x capacity + 2.5x training all stayed in 0.3-0.5 SSIM). recon_dcstep_every is the LAST untried mechanism that could falsify this: a Resample-style FULL hard-CG projection (relax=1.0) onto the measurement manifold is a STRONGER fidelity backstop than the soft DPS gradient -- it directly minimizes ||A x_mu - y||^2 by n_cg Gauss-Newton steps every 5 reverse steps, re-noising back to t_next. If the prior were merely under-guided, hard-DC would pull the recon decisively toward the sino and clear (or approach) the FBP floor; if the prior is structurally mismatched, the re-noise step injects the mismatched prior right back and the recon stays in the 0.37-0.42 band regardless. BUDGET MATH (HARD 20-min = 1200s wall, val=ALL 214 L277 slices): calibrated linear cost from the two measured points (iter-2 25-step every=0 = 4.058 s/slice; iter-3 32-step every=0 = 5.158 s/slice) gives per-step a=0.1572 s/step/slice + fixed offset b=0.127 s/slice, so one projector call ~ a/3 = 0.0524 s/call/slice. At n_steps=25, warmup=5, every=5 the DC-step triggers at k=5,10,15,20 (4 triggers, t_next>0), each adding n_cg=2 * (2 fwd + 1 back) = 6 projector calls = 6*0.0524 = 0.314 s/slice/trigger -> +1.26 s/slice total. Per-slice = 4.06 + 1.26 = 5.32 s -> 214 * 5.32 = 1137 s = 19.0 min < 1200 s wall (~63 s headroom, MORE in practice since the fixed offset b does not scale with DC). n_cg=3 (1272s=21.2min) or n_steps=28 (1306s) or every=4 (1205s) all BLOW the wall, so n_steps=25 / every=5 / n_cg=2 is the LARGEST hard-DC dose that fits -- the right budget-feasible probe. SIX-BOX PREDICTION: SSIM <= 0.42, hr = 0 (the structural-prior-mismatch hypothesis). FALSIFIER: if SSIM CLEARS the 0.8078 LD-FBP floor (or moves decisively toward it, say >0.6), the Mayo v4 DDPM prior was NOT structurally mismatched -- it was fidelity-starved, and hard-DC is the fix; redirect future iters to tuning the hard-DC dose (relax/n_cg/every). If SSIM STAYS in the 0.37-0.42 band (FBP floor uncleared even with full hard-CG fidelity), FILE THE DIFFUSION-PRIOR-MISMATCH VERDICT: the lever is the prior CLASS, not any sampler/fidelity hyperparameter (mirrors the breast-DDPM hr=0 decision), STOP iterating diffusion-recon on Mayo, and the BEST run stays iter-2 (SSIM 0.396, hr 0). val=ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV (default -- not passing fov=False).
